1	# microgpt iteration 2: plan for the from-scratch notation exploration
2	
3	Approved by Pavol 2026-08-26. This file is the complete context for every
4	worker in the run. Read it fully before doing anything.
5	
6	## Mission (approved verbatim in essence)
7	
8	Test Fortress's founding claim on the best possible specimen. The claim:
9	the gap between how ML literature states a transformer's mathematics and
10	how programs implement it is a language defect that Fortress was built
11	to close. The specimen: Karpathy's microgpt, the smallest complete GPT.
12	The test: construct, in running and verified Fortress, the notation that
13	lets each building block of the model be stated so that its typeset form
14	and the literature's own formula sit side by side and the reader can
15	judge the distance **by eye**. The deliverable teaches two things at
16	once and inseparably: how a GPT works (a reader starting from zero
17	leaves understanding it) and how the notation is constructed (what the
18	language gives, what it must be taught, and what it cannot yet say).
19	Where the correspondence fails, the failure is shown and classified —
20	implementation gap (revival worklist) versus design limit. Everything
21	shown runs; correctness is anchored to the Python reference; the
22	process is documented.
23	
24	**Not the mission** (named local minima — do not fall into them):
25	fidelity to Steele's 2015 slide idioms; preservation of any prior
26	rung's code structure (this iteration starts FROM SCRATCH); the golden
27	check as an aesthetic constraint (it is a correctness instrument only);
28	interpreter speed (measured, reported, never steering notation).
29	
30	## Standing design rules (from Pavol, binding)
31	
32	1. **No custom BIG operators** (`BIG OPLUS`, `BIG BOXPLUS`, any new
33	   glyph) unless the form is (a) genuinely the prevalent way ML
34	   literature writes that mathematics, or (b) provably the only working
35	   way in current Fortress, with the spec-vs-implementation gap
36	   documented. The ML literature writes Σ, Π, 𝔼, max — never custom big
37	   operators. Glyph imitation of Σ is not Σ. Default: named functions
38	   (`sum(...)`) over comprehensions; the genuine library `SUM` where
39	   summands are `Number`s (e.g. over `.data` inside a sum-node
40	   constructor).
41	2. **The specification is the first authority** for any language
42	   question: `Specification/` LaTeX sources (byte-identical to
43	   1.0-frozen in all chapters audited so far). Order of authority:
44	   spec → `explorations/expressiveness-review.md` (audited findings
45	   with probes) → library sources → fresh empirical probe. Never end a
46	   design path at the first interpreter error: check what the spec
47	   sanctions (the vector×matrix "impossibility" had a documented
48	   escape, the Meet Rule / `excludes`), then record divergence.
49	3. **No single-data-point rules.** Any claimed constraint ("always
50	   parenthesize X", "Y is impossible") requires either a spec citation
51	   or two independent probes, recorded.
52	
53	## Verified facts (do not re-derive; probes in `explorations/spec-probes/`)
54	
55	- List/comprehension element-type ascriptions `[\T\]` are needed ONLY
56	  when elements' runtime class differs from the target (numeric
57	  literals → `FloatLiteral`; nested `ArrayList[\…\]` under invariant
58	  `List`). For concrete object element types (like an autodiff node)
59	  they are redundant. Return types on definitions are optional
60	  (inference chapter in the spec is a stub; the implementation infers).
61	  The `zip` static argument is mandatory.
62	- The algebraic tower that exists: `AdditiveGroup[\T\]` and
63	  `MultiplicativeRing[\T\]` only (`FortressLibrary.fss:328,340`).
64	  Extending `MultiplicativeRing[\V\]` with `one`/`TIMES` inherits
65	  juxtaposition, binary minus, `zero` (precedent:
66	  `explorations/complex_ring.fss`). The spec's full
67	  `Monoid…Field` chapter ships only as commented-out
68	  `Library/incomplete/…INCOMPLETE`.
69	- Two juxtaposition (or any operator) overloads on `(List,List)` shapes
70	  are illegal — but **mutually excluding carrier traits make both
71	  directions legal** (library's own Vector/Matrix at
72	  `FortressLibrary.fss:2634,2641` via `Rank1 excludes Rank2`; probes
73	  `p7_excludes.fss`, `p14_genwrap.fss` — a six-line carrier object also
74	  buys `|x|`, `x[i]`, `x[r]`, generator integration, `.map`, clean
75	  renders).
76	- `SUM` is closed to user types three ways (library `Number` seal,
77	  spec's no-static-param-overloading rule, desugarer's one-nullary-
78	  registration-per-name). Coercion parses but is unwired. Multifix
79	  dispatch is unimplemented. `Number` already has `SQRT`.
80	- Real parse traps (verified): chained subscripts need `(m[i])[j]`
81	  (grammatical by design, `concrete-syntax.tex:921`); `^` after a call
82	  or dotted field needs parens; `|w||>` and `/|` need a space; `V`
83	  cannot name a variable while object `V` is in scope. FALSIFIED trap,
84	  do not propagate: "comprehension bodies ending in a subscript need
85	  parens" — they don't.
86	- Interpreter performance law: run everything `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`
87	  (idle-worker micro-forking makes 2 workers slower than 1).
88	- `nat`-parameterized user vectors with dimension-checked ops run
89	  (`p9_natvec.fss`) — available as a design ingredient, not a mandate.
90	
91	## Correctness anchors
92	
93	- The golden check: deterministic-weight config in
94	  `explorations/microgpt.fss` `goldenCheck()` — 15 logits + mean loss
95	  1.228662661701597 + 5 gradients at 1e-9. Any complete candidate must
96	  pass it (values are architecture-level truths, independent of
97	  notation). Nucleus-stage candidates use the lighter analytic checks
98	  (style of `explorations/mgnative_a.fss` run()) or hand-computed
99	  attention values.
100	- Reference implementations for BEHAVIOR only (not style):
101	  `explorations/microgpt.fss` (v1), `microgpt_native.fss`,
102	  `microgpt_paper.fss`. Architecture facts: 1 layer, heads structural,
103	  rmsnorm without gain, no biases, plain relu, causal by history,
104	  Adam β₁ .85 β₂ .99 lr .01 linear decay, BOS=26 vocab 27.
105	
106	## Fitness function
107	
108	For each building block, typeset the Fortress definition with Fortify
109	(recipe in any `explorations/fortify/*.tic` header: fortick → latex →
110	dvisvgm; rasterize with chromium `--headless --no-sandbox --screenshot`)
111	and hold it against the literature's formula for that block:
112	
113	- h⁰ = Wₑ[t] + Wₚ[i]
114	- RMSNorm(x) = x / √(x·x/d + ε)
115	- A(q,kⱼ) = q·kⱼ/√d_k ; weights = softmax over j≤i ; out = Σⱼ pⱼvⱼ
116	  (vector form: softmax(qKᵀ/√d_k)V)
117	- FFN(x) = W₂ relu(W₁ x)
118	- L = −log softmax(logits)_y
119	- Adam: element-wise update equations (index form IS the literature here)
120	
121	Judged by eye: would a reader of the paper recognize the line? Every
122	departure needs a reason from the classification {implementation gap,
123	design limit, deliberate-with-reason}.
124	
125	## Deliverables ladder (this workflow: nucleus stage)
126	
127	Each design candidate delivers a NUCLEUS, not the full model: the
128	notation layer it proposes plus running, checked implementations of
129	rmsnorm, softmax, one-head attention (score+weights+blend over a
130	history), and ffn, over the candidate's own autodiff value type (a
131	minimal tape engine is fine; reuse of engine A's *concepts* is allowed,
132	code written fresh). Plus: its Fortify render sheet, a rasterized PNG,
133	and a design memo (what the language gave / had to be taught / can't
134	say; every deviation classified; what the full model would look like —
135	sketch the forward pass in the candidate's notation).
136	
137	Full-model implementation, presentation build, and integration happen
138	AFTER Pavol-side judgment of the candidates — not in this workflow.
139	
140	## Presentation (context for memos; built after judgment)
141	
142	The rebuilt page interleaves tightly: short concept prose per block,
143	then immediately the paired lines — the literature's formula and the
144	Fortress definition's render, adjacent, no repetition of the formula in
145	prose, no tan "the paper writes" echo boxes, never a big code block
146	followed by explanation. New content queued: the honest-loss-curve
147	section (explorations/training-dynamics.md + chart) and the
148	PRNG/SplitMix lineage note (Fortress's parallelism → Steele's 2014
149	splittable PRNGs; explorations/prng-findings.md). The three prior rungs
150	(transliteration → index → carriers) remain the notation-ladder
151	exhibit.
152	
153	## Worker discipline
154	
155	Worktree only; `ant compileAll` once (env per CLAUDE.md: JDK 25
156	exports, unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, FORTRESS_HOME=$PWD); no commits, no
157	pushes, no tracked-file modifications; deliverables copied to the
158	session scratchpad under your candidate's name; timings indicative
159	(shared box). Report every dead end with the error verbatim and the
160	spec section consulted.

2	import List.{...}
3	export Executable
4	
5	(* The library's own answer to "vector times matrix AND matrix times vector":
6	   Vector extends Rank1, Matrix extends Rank2, and
7	     trait Rank1 extends {Rank[\1\]} excludes { Rank2, Rank3, Number, String }
8	   (FortressLibrary.fss:1599).  The EXCLUSION is what makes the overload pair
9	   legal -- not any property of the generic instantiation.  Reproduce it for
10	   List-carried vectors with a one-field wrapper. *)
11	
12	object V(var data: RR64) getter asString(): String = "V(" data ")" end
13	
14	trait Rank1V excludes Rank2V end
15	trait Rank2V excludes Rank1V end
16	
17	object Vec(xs: List[\V\]) extends Rank1V
18	  getter asString(): String = "Vec" xs
19	  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
20	  opr [i: ZZ32]: V = xs[i]
21	end
22	object Mat(rows: List[\Vec\]) extends Rank2V
23	  getter asString(): String = "Mat" rows
24	  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |rows|
25	  opr [i: ZZ32]: Vec = rows[i]
26	end
27	
28	opr DOT(u: Vec, w: Vec): V = V(SUM[m <- seq(0#|u|)] (u[m].data w[m].data))
29	(* BOTH directions, the pair the paper file could not declare on raw Lists *)
30	opr juxtaposition(m: Mat, x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<|[\V\] (m[r] DOT x) | r <- 0#|m| |>)
31	opr juxtaposition(p: Vec, m: Mat): Vec =
32	  Vec(<|[\V\] (V(SUM[j <- seq(0#|p|)] (p[j].data (m[j])[c].data))) | c <- 0#|m[0]| |>)

398	
399	The journal's "P3, why `SUM` is closed" concluded impossibility. Both halves of
400	the answer are now precise, and the *reason* differs from what was recorded.
401	
402	**(i) Library sealing, not spec design.** `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3041`:
403	
404	```
405	opr SUM[\T extends Number\](): Comprehension[\T,Number,Number,Number\] = …
406	```

419	> for one declaration to have static parameters and another to not have them.

export Executable

(* mgcarriers.fss -- design candidate "carriers" for microgpt iteration 2
   (explorations/microgpt-iteration2-plan.md).  NUCLEUS: typed vector and

   four building blocks -- rmsnorm, softmax, one-head attention, ffn --
   each stated at model level with ZERO visible loops or comprehensions
   and BOTH juxtaposition directions:  W x  (matrix times vector) and
   p V  (attention weights times value matrix).

   The autodiff node is named Value, as in Karpathy's Python -- which
   frees the letter V for the value matrix at model level (a variable
   cannot be named V while an OBJECT V is in scope; renaming the engine
   type dissolves the clash instead of working around it).

   Checks: hand-computed forward values for every block, plus central
   finite-difference gradient checks of the whole tape through each
   block (h = 1e-6, tolerance 1e-4 absolute). *)

(* ---------- scalar reverse-mode autodiff: the tape engine ---------- *)

(* Value is a multiplicative ring; saying so buys juxtaposition (= TIMES),
   binary minus (= self + (-o)) and zero as trait defaults
   (precedent: explorations/complex_ring.fss). *)
object Value(var data: RR64, children: List[\Value\], grads: List[\RR64\])
       extends MultiplicativeRing[\Value\]
  getter one(): Value = konst(1.0)
  getter asString(): String = "" data
  var grad: RR64 := 0.0
  var visited: Boolean := false
  opr +(self, o: Value): Value = Value(data + o.data, <| self, o |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0, 1.0|>)
  opr +(self, c: RR64): Value = Value(data + c, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0|>)
  opr TIMES(self, o: Value): Value =
    Value(data o.data, <| self, o |>, <|[\RR64\] o.data, data|>)
  opr -(self): Value = Value(-data, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] -1.0|>)
  opr -(self, c: RR64): Value = Value(data - c, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0|>)
  opr /(self, o: Value): Value =
    Value(data / o.data, <| self, o |>,
          <|[\RR64\] 1.0 / o.data, (-data) / (o.data o.data)|>)
  opr /(self, c: RR64): Value = Value(data / c, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0 / c|>)
  opr /(self, n: ZZ32): Value = self / (n 1.0)
  opr ^(self, n: RR64): Value = Value(data^n, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] n data^(n-1.0)|>)
end

konst(d: RR64): Value = Value(d, emptyList[\Value\](), emptyList[\RR64\]())

exp(v: Value): Value = Value(exp v.data, <| v |>, <|[\RR64\] exp v.data|>)
log(v: Value): Value = Value(log v.data, <| v |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0/v.data|>)
relu(v: Value): Value = if v.data > 0.0

   sum/Sigma; the plan's rule 1 prefers sum(...) over a custom BIG glyph):
   d(sum)/d(addend_i) = 1, forward value one sequential fold at the leaf. *)
sum(addends: List[\Value\]): Value =
  Value(SUM[a <- seq(addends)] a.data, addends, <|[\RR64\] 1.0 | a <- addends|>)

object Topo()

  build(v: Value): () = do
    if NOT v.visited then
      v.visited := true
      for ch <- seq(v.children) do self.build(ch) end
      items := items.addRight(v)
    end

end

  root.grad := 1.0

trait Rank1V excludes Rank2V end

  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0#|xs|
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: Value = xs[i]
  opr [r: Range[\ZZ32\]]: ZeroIndexed[\Value\] = Vec(xs[r])

opr DOT(u: Vec, w: Vec): Value = sum(<| (u[m] w[m]) | m <- u.indices |>)

(* componentwise vector algebra *)
opr +(x: Vec, y: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| (x[m] + y[m]) | m <- x.indices |>)
opr -(x: Vec, c: RR64): Vec = Vec(<| (u - c) | u <- x |>)
opr /(x: Vec, s: Value): Vec = Vec(<| (u / s) | u <- x |>)
opr /(x: Vec, c: RR64): Vec = Vec(<| (u / c) | u <- x |>)
relu(x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| (relu u) | u <- x |>)
exp(x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| (exp u) | u <- x |>)
sum(x: Vec): Value = sum(x.xs)
max(x: Vec): RR64 = BIG MAX[u <- x] u.data

(* ---------- the model blocks: zero loops, zero comprehensions ---------- *)

(* RMSNorm(x) = x / SQRT(x DOT x / d + eps) -- no learnable gain *)
rmsnorm(x: Vec): Vec = x / SQRT((x DOT x)/|x| + 0.00001)

(* softmax(a)_j = e^(a_j - c) / SUM_k e^(a_k - c);  c = max a is an RR64
   constant: softmax(a) = softmax(a - c) is an identity, so the shift
   carries no gradient by mathematics, not by accident. *)
softmax(a: Vec): Vec = do
  e = exp(a - max(a))
  e / sum(e)
end

(* attention at one step over the history:  out = softmax(K q / SQRT d_k) V.
   K q is the score vector (K q)_j = k_j DOT q = q DOT k_j -- the same
   numbers the paper writes q K^T.  K and V hold keys/values of positions
   0..i only, so causality is the data, not a mask. *)
attend(q: Vec, K: Mat, V: Mat): Vec = softmax((K q) / SQRT |q|) V

(* FFN(x) = W2 relu(W1 x) *)
ffn(x: Vec, W1: Mat, W2: Mat): Vec = W2 relu(W1 x)

(* ---------- checks ---------- *)

mkVec(ds: List[\RR64\]): Vec = Vec(<| (konst(d)) | d <- ds |>)
row2(a: RR64, b: RR64): Vec = mkVec(<|[\RR64\] a, b|>)

(* central finite-difference gradient check of scalar f over leaf vector *)
fdcheck(name: String, f: Vec -> Value, xs: List[\RR64\]): () = do
  lx = mkVec(xs)
  y = f(lx)
  backward(y)
  h = 0.000001
  for i <- seq(0#|xs|) do
    xp = <|[\RR64\] (if j = i then xs[j] + h else xs[j] end) | j <- 0#|xs| |>
    xm = <|[\RR64\] (if j = i then xs[j] - h else xs[j] end) | j <- 0#|xs| |>
    num = (f(mkVec(xp)).data - f(mkVec(xm)).data) / (2.0 h)
    assert(|lx[i].grad - num| < 0.0001, name " grad " i " analytic " lx[i].grad " numeric " num)
  end
  println(name " gradients vs central differences: PASS")
end

  tol = 10.0^(-9)

  (* --- carrier algebra: both juxtaposition directions, by hand --- *)
  x = row2(1.0, 2.0)
  m = Mat(<| row2(1.0, 2.0), row2(3.0, 4.0) |>)
  mx = m x
  xm = x m
  assert(|mx[0].data - 5.0| < tol, "m x [0]")
  assert(|mx[1].data - 11.0| < tol, "m x [1]")
  assert(|xm[0].data - 7.0| < tol, "x m [0]")
  assert(|xm[1].data - 10.0| < tol, "x m [1]")
  assert(|((x DOT x).data) - 5.0| < tol, "x DOT x")
  assert(|x| = 2, "size")
  println("carriers: W x and p V both directions: PASS")

  (* --- rmsnorm: x=(3,4), d=2: x/SQRT(25/2 + 1e-5) --- *)
  r1 = rmsnorm(row2(3.0, 4.0))
  d1 = SQRT (12.5 + 0.00001)
  assert(|r1[0].data - 3.0/d1| < tol, "rmsnorm[0]")
  assert(|r1[1].data - 4.0/d1| < tol, "rmsnorm[1]")
  println("rmsnorm forward: PASS")

  (* --- softmax: a=(0, ln 2, ln 3) -> (1/6, 1/3, 1/2) --- *)
  s1 = softmax(mkVec(<|[\RR64\] 0.0, log 2.0, log 3.0|>))
  assert(|s1[0].data - 1.0/6.0| < tol, "softmax[0]")
  assert(|s1[1].data - 1.0/3.0| < tol, "softmax[1]")
  assert(|s1[2].data - 1.0/2.0| < tol, "softmax[2]")
  println("softmax forward: PASS")

  (* --- attention: q=(2,0); keys (1,0),(0,1); values (3,1),(1,5).
     scores = (2/SQRT 2, 0);  p = softmax;  out = p0 (3,1) + p1 (1,5) --- *)

  Kh = Mat(<| row2(1.0, 0.0), row2(0.0, 1.0) |>)
  Vh = Mat(<| row2(3.0, 1.0), row2(1.0, 5.0) |>)

  s0 = 2.0 / (SQRT 2.0)
  z = exp s0

  p1 = 1.0 / (z + 1.0)

  assert(|a1[1].data - (p0 + 5.0 p1)| < tol, "attend[1]")

     W1 x = (-1,4) -> relu (0,4) -> W2 . = (4,8) --- *)

  W2 = Mat(<| row2(1.0, 1.0), row2(0.0, 2.0) |>)

  assert(|f1[1].data - 8.0| < tol, "ffn[1]")

Fortress specifies that certain operators have higher precedence than
certain other operators and certain operators are associative,
so that one need not use parentheses in all
cases where operators are mixed in an expression.  (See
\appref{operator-precedence} for a detailed description of operator
precedence and associativity in Fortress.)  However, Fortress
does not follow the practice of other programming languages in
simply assigning an integer to each operator and then saying that
the precedence of any two operators can be compared by comparing
their assigned integers.  Instead, Fortress relies on defining traditional
groups of operators based on their meaning and shape, and specifies
specific precedence relationships between some of these groups.
If there is no specific precedence relationship between two
operators, then parentheses must be used.  For example, Fortress
does not accept the expression \EXP{a + b \cup c};
one must write either \EXP{(a + b) \cup c} or \EXP{a + (b \cup c)}.
(Whether or not the result then makes any sense depends on what definitions
have been made for the \EXP{+} and \EXP{\cup} operators---see
\chapref{operatordefs}.)

....
The boolean operators

The arithmetic and relational operators are further divided into groups based on shape:

\boxplus \boxminus \boxdot \boxtimes < \leq \geq > \ll \lll \ggg \gg

\subsection{Identifiers}
\seclabel{render-identifiers}

Fortress has rather complicated rules for rendering an identifier;
as in other parts of Fortress, the rules are complicated so that
the simple cases will be very simple, but also so that difficult
cases of interest will be possible.

It is conventional in mathematical notation to make use of variables,
particularly single-letter variables, in a number of different fonts or styles,
with italic being the most common, then boldface, and roman:
\VAR{a}, \EXP{\mathbf{b}}, \EXP{\mathrm{c}}.  Frequently such variables
are also decorated with accents and subscripts:
\EXP{\bar{\VAR{p}}}, \EXP{q'}, \EXP{\hat{\VAR{r}}}, \EXP{T_{\mathrm{max}}}, \EXP{\vec{\mathbf{u}}},
\EXP{\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{x}}}, \EXP{w_{17}}, \EXP{\bar{\VAR{z}}_{17}'}.
Fortress provides conventions for typing such variables using
plain ASCII characters: for example, the unformatted presentations of these same
variables are \STR{a}, \STR{{\char'137}b}, \STR{c{\char'137}},
\STR{p{\char'137}bar}, \STR{q'} or \STR{q{\char'137}prime}, \STR{r{\char'137}hat},

# Candidate "carriers" — design memo

Nucleus: `mgcarriers.fss` (runs green, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`, ~4 s wall
including JVM startup). Render sheet: `mgcarriers-forms.tic` →
`mgcarriers-forms-{light,dark}.svg`, rasterized `mgcarriers-forms.png`.
Probe added this session: `pc_nat.fss`. Everything below was run on the
worktree build (`ant compileAll`, JDK 25, exit 0).

## The design in one paragraph

Vectors and matrices are six-to-nine-line carrier objects (`Vec`, `Mat`)
on mutually excluding rank traits — the library's own Vector/Matrix
pattern (`Rank1 excludes Rank2`, FortressLibrary.fss:1599). The
exclusion is what makes BOTH juxtaposition directions legal at once
(`W x` matrix–vector and `p V` vector–matrix), which is exactly the pair
the bare-`List` design of `microgpt_paper.fss` could not declare and
papered over with `BIG BOXPLUS`. The autodiff node is named `Value`
(Karpathy's own class name), which frees the letter `V` for the value
matrix at model level — the prior rung's `Vv` wart dissolves by renaming
the engine type, not by working around it. On top of the carriers, every
notation-layer operator is defined once by its index formula; the model
blocks are then loop-free, comprehension-free lines. The nucleus
contains **zero custom BIG operators** (standing rule 1 satisfied in
full: the only big operator is the library's `BIG MAX` over `RR64`
inside `max`; n-ary summation is the named function `sum(...)`, one tape
node). The `BIG OPLUS`/`BIG BOXPLUS`/`VConcat`/`VecConcat` machinery of
the prior rung — some 20 lines and two invented glyphs — is not needed
at all in this design: `sum` subsumes both.

## Block-by-block: render vs. literature (judge by the PNG)

| block | literature | this candidate renders | distance |
|---|---|---|---|
| RMSNorm | x / √(x·x/d + ε) | x / √((x·x)/\|x\| + ε) | parens on (x·x) forced (see D1); \|x\| for d |
| softmax | e^{a_j} / Σ_k e^{a_k} | e = exp(a − max(a)); e/sum(e) | max-shift shown (stabilization, an identity); sum(e) not Σ_k (D4) |
| attention | softmax(qKᵀ/√d_k)V | softmax(K q/√d_k) V | K q instead of qKᵀ (D2); d_k bound to \|q\| one line above |
| FFN | W₂ relu(W₁ x) | **W**₂ relu(**W**₁ x) | exact (bold weights via `_W1`; typical paper typography) |
| h⁰ (sketch) | Wₑ[t] + Wₚ[i] | `_Wte[t] + _Wpe[i]` | exact shape; names longer |

`attend` is the headline: `softmax(K q / SQRT d_k) V` is a genuine
one-expression line — score, weights and blend, with the causal mask
being the data (K, V hold positions 0..i only), and both juxtaposition
directions in a single expression.

## What the language gave (for free or nearly)

- Both juxtaposition directions, from a 2-line `excludes` pair — spec's
  Meet Rule (`advanced/overloading.tex`), library precedent.
- `|x|`, `x[i]`, `x[r]`, `u <- x` generators, `for r <- m` — from
  `ZeroIndexed`/`DelegatedIndexed` on the carriers (probe p14 pattern).
- Juxtaposition, binary minus, `zero` on `Value` from
  `MultiplicativeRing[\Value\]` (complex_ring precedent).
- Rendering conventions that turn ASCII into the paper's typography,
  discovered by probing fortick (`idtest.tic`, kept in the render dir):
  `epsilon` → ε, `d_k` → d_k (subscript), `_W1` → **W**₁ (bold,
  subscripted — the leading-underscore-is-boldface convention of
  `basic/lexical-structure.tex` §render-identifiers), `m[0]` → m₀,
  `u[m] w[m]` → u_m w_m. All of these are legal interpreter identifiers
  (verified by the green run).
- `SQRT` on dimensions via library `Number.SQRT` (`SQRT d_k` with
  `d_k: ZZ32`).

## What the language had to be taught (the machinery bill)

Notation layer, 22 lines total (counting signatures, not comments):

- carriers: 2 (rank traits) + 8 (`Vec`) + 9 (`Mat`) = 19 lines — but
  these also replace the prior rung's 20-line big-operator/monoid
  machinery, so the trade is roughly line-neutral and glyph-negative
  (two invented glyphs removed).
- operators: `DOT` 1, `Mat Vec` juxtaposition 1, `Vec Mat` juxtaposition
  2, elementwise `+ − / /` 4, `relu`/`exp` lifts 2, `sum(Vec)` 1,
  `max(Vec)` 1 = 12 lines, each a one-line index formula that is itself
  an exhibit (the renders read as definitions: (W x)_r = W_r · x).

Engine (below notation): ~55 lines — `Value` ring object, `konst`,
`exp/log/relu/SQRT`, the n-ary `sum` node, `Topo`, `backward`. Fresh
code; concepts shared with engine A as permitted.

## What it cannot say (deviations, classified)

- **D1 — `(x·x)/|x|` needs parens.** Unparenthesized `x DOT x / |x|`
  fails: *"Loose operators DOT and / have incomparable precedence"*
  (error verbatim). Spec consulted: `basic/operators/precedence.tex` —
  Fortress precedence is deliberately a partial order ("If there is no
  specific precedence relationship between two operators, then
  parentheses must be used"); the appendix (`appendices/operators.tex`
  §Multiplication and Division) makes multiplication operators
  left-associative *among themselves* and division nonassociative, with
  no mult/div mixing relation. **Design limit (deliberate language
  design), not a bug**: the paper's x·x/d leans on a human convention
  Fortress refuses to guess. Juxtaposition, by contrast, *is* ordered
  above `/`, which is why `K q / SQRT d_k` needs no parens.
- **D2 — `K q` instead of `qKᵀ`.** No transpose operator is defined
  here; (K q)_j = k_j·q = q·k_j, so the numbers are identical and the
  render is honest. Classified **deliberate-with-reason**: a `q Kt`
  spelling via a transpose getter would be *farther* from the paper than
  `K q`, and several formulations of attention (column-vector
  convention) write Kq. A true postfix ᵀ is not expressible as an
  operator on the carrier today (no postfix-superscript operator form) —
  that part is a **design limit**.
- **D3 — `d_k = |q|` is a binding, not a given.** In the nucleus,
  attend is a free function, so d_k is bound from the query's length in
  the line above (making attend a 2-line do-block). In the full model
  attend becomes a method and `d_k` a config field, restoring the
  one-liner. **Deliberate**, dissolves at full-model stage.
- **D4 — `sum(...)`/`max(...)` are named functions, not Σ/max-big-op.**
  Σ over tape values cannot be the library `SUM` (sealed to `Number`
  three independent ways — audit finding 7), and a custom `BIG OPLUS`
  is banned by standing rule 1. The named function is the rule's own
  default. In renders, `sum(⟨u_m w_m | m ← u.indices⟩)` appears in the
  *notation layer only*; model level never shows a comprehension.
  Classified **deliberate (rule 1)**, with the underlying closure of Σ
  an **implementation/library gap** already on the revival worklist.
- **D5 — `W_1` is not a legal identifier** (interpreter: `Syntax Error`
  at the parameter position; digit directly after underscore). Spec
  consulted: `basic/lexical-structure.tex` §render-identifiers gives
  `w17`, `T_max`, `_v` as the ASCII conventions — underscore-then-letter
  is sanctioned (`d_k` works), underscore-then-digit is not in its
  example set, so this is at worst **spec-silent, implementation
  refuses**. The bold `_W1` → **W**₁ convention is the spec-sanctioned
  escape and arguably *better* (papers bold their weight matrices).
- **D6 — capital-plus-digit renders roman.** `W1` renders as upright
  `W1` (fortify treats capitalized mixed names as type names), while
  `w1` → w₁. So italic-capital W₁ is unreachable; bold **W**₁ (D5) is
  the closest paper form. **Toolchain (Fortify) limit**, not a language
  limit.
- **D7 — `(m[j])[c]` chained-subscript parens** in the Vec–Mat
  juxtaposition definition: grammatical by design
  (`concrete-syntax.tex:921`, already on record). Notation layer only.
  **Design limit (known)**.

## nat-dimension parameters (p9): REJECTED, with evidence

Probe `pc_nat.fss`: instantiating `mk[\k\]` where `k: ZZ32 = 3` fails
with **"k is undefined."** (verbatim) — static `nat` arguments must be
static; the model's dimensions (vocab, nEmbd, headSize) are runtime
config values, so `Vec[\n\]`-style carriers cannot even be *constructed*
on the model's real data path, only on literal-dimension toys
(p9 passes with `mk[\3\]`). Second reason: every notation-layer
signature would grow `[\nat n\]` static clutter, moving the renders
*away* from the paper register (papers say q ∈ ℝ^{d_k} once, in prose).
Third: the shape errors nat-checking would catch are already caught by
the golden check. Echoes audit finding 13's verdict; the nat-shaped
`microgpt_dim.fss` remains a reachable spec-shaped *destination*, not
this rung.

## Checks (all green)

- Both juxtaposition directions against hand-computed 2×2 values.
- rmsnorm forward: x=(3,4) against √(12.5+ε) by hand.
- softmax forward: (0, ln 2, ln 3) → (1/6, 1/3, 1/2).
- attention forward: q=(2,0), K=((1,0),(0,1)), V=((3,1),(1,5)) against
  the closed-form softmax(√2, 0) blend.
- ffn forward: one negative pre-activation exercises the relu kink.
- Gradient of every block: central finite differences (h=1e−6) against
  the tape, through a fixed linear probe r·block(x); rmsnorm, softmax,
  attend (d/dq), ffn all within 1e−4.

## The full model in this notation (forward-pass sketch, not yet run)

```fortress
object Model(vocab: ZZ32, nHead: ZZ32, d_k: ZZ32,
             _Wte: Mat, _Wpe: Mat, _Wlm: Mat,
             _Wq: List[\Mat\], _Wk: List[\Mat\], _Wv: List[\Mat\],
             _Wo: Mat, _W1: Mat, _W2: Mat)

  attend(q: Vec, K: Mat, V: Mat): Vec = softmax(K q / SQRT d_k) V

  ffn(x: Vec): Vec = _W2 relu(_W1 x)

  forward(t: ZZ32, i: ZZ32, kh: List[\Mat\], vh: List[\Mat\])
      : (Vec, List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]) = do
    h0 = _Wte[t] + _Wpe[i]
    x1 = rmsnorm(h0)
    x2 = rmsnorm(x1)
    K = <| (kh[h]).addRight(_Wk[h] x2) | h <- 0#nHead |>
    V = <| (vh[h]).addRight(_Wv[h] x2) | h <- 0#nHead |>
    heads = <| attend(_Wq[h] x2, K[h], V[h]) | h <- 0#nHead |>
    x4 = _Wo concat(heads) + x1
    x6 = ffn(rmsnorm(x4)) + x4
    (_Wlm x6, K, V)
  end
end

nll(logits: Vec, y: ZZ32): Value = do
  p = softmax(logits)
  -(log (p[y]))
end
```

Notes on the sketch: (i) `attend` regains its one-line form because
`d_k` is a Model field; (ii) the three per-head comprehensions are the
one place comprehensions surface at model level — they are the
literature's own "head₁ … head_h" ellipsis made precise, classified
deliberate; if judged too loud, `K`,`V`,`heads` can move behind a
`Heads` carrier with its own map, at the cost of more carrier lines;
(iii) `concat(heads: List[\Vec\]): Vec` and `+(Vec, Vec)` (already in
the nucleus) are the only notation-layer additions the full model needs;
(iv) history matrices are per-head `Mat`s extended by `addRight` — the
KV cache is visible as data; (v) inside `Model`, locals named `K` and
`V` coexist with `attend`'s parameters of the same names, and `V` stays
free because the engine node is `Value`; (vi) Adam stays index-form
`RR64` (its literature form IS elementwise index arithmetic); (vii) the
golden check carries over unchanged — its numbers are architecture
truths.

## Dead ends, verbatim (worker discipline)

1. `x / SQRT((x DOT x)/|x| + …)` — `Unmatched delimiters "(" and "/|"`:
   the known `/|` lexing trap; space fixes it.
2. `x DOT x / |x|` — `Loose operators DOT and / have incomparable
   precedence.` Spec: `basic/operators/precedence.tex` (partial order by
   design) + `appendices/operators.tex` §multdivops. Kept parens.
3. `ffn(x: Vec, W_1: Mat, …)` — `Syntax Error` at the identifier:
   underscore-digit. Spec: `basic/lexical-structure.tex`
   §render-identifiers; switched to `_W1` (bold render, legal).
4. `mk[\k\]` with runtime `k` — `k is undefined.` (pc_nat.fss). Spec:
   static parameters are static (`basic/trait-parameters.tex`). Grounds
   for rejecting nat-dimension carriers at model scale.
